newsitem.title: USA: Bond syndicates must be savvy about muni rules - PSA.
newsitem.headline: Bond syndicates must be savvy about muni rules - PSA.

text.p: Firms that want to join municipal bond syndicates would have to pledge to comply with recent rules aimed at improving the amount of data available to potential bond investors, according to a draft plan circulated by bond dealers Friday.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association is requesting comments on that and other proposed revisions to its six-year-old master "Agreement Among Underwriters" or AAU, by September 15.
When securities firms come together to sell a particular muni bond deal, they form a "syndicate."
Syndicate members sign a detailed pact, called an AAU, that sets out how the group will operate.

For instance, firms must certify that they understand and will comply with rules enacted by the Securities and Exchange Commission and Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board that affect the sale of muni bonds.
New rules, for instance, require dealers to certify that they will circulate draft and final prospectuses, called official statements, to interested investors within a certain number of days.

Firms in a syndicate also would have to certify that they have not been barred from underwriting an issuer's bonds because of inappropriate political contributions to elected officials of the particular state or locality.
MSRB's rule G-37 bars muni bond dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.

Syndicate members also would have to certify that they will comply with MSRB's revised rule G-36, which requires them to send copies of official statements to the MSRB and a series of private information libraries across the nation, according to the draft.
